findings.title: ADR-0008's 'bounded sink' list (head -c N, wc, grep -c, jq with a scalar ...) is still open-ended and jq cannot be decided statically, unresolved since r2
findings.claim: 'Allow when ... the pipeline ends in a bounded sink (head -c N, wc, grep -c, jq with a scalar ...)'

archaeology.method: grep for 'jq' and 'bounded sink' across DECISIONS-r3.md, REVIEW-r3.md, ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md, BOTTLENECKS-r3.md, OWNER-QUESTIONS-r3.md, REVIEW-r4a.md, ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r4.md, BOTTLENECKS-r4.md — zero hits in all of them
archaeology.introduced_by: doc-only text, raised already in out/r2/round1/review/algorithms.json finding at ADR-0008:25 ('ambiguity', severity major): 'no numeric bound... jq with a scalar cannot be decided without a jq program analysis'
archaeology.original_intent: the sink list is meant to let a curl|jq pipeline pass when the HTTP body does not reach stdout as raw text
archaeology.regression_risk: a static parser cannot know at decide-time whether a given jq filter produces a scalar (depends on the filter program and the runtime JSON shape); 'jq with a scalar' is not decidable from argv0 + flags the way the rest of the parser works. The owner rule is 'no fallback chains; no regex or truncation as a decision mechanism' — an underspecified sink list risks being patched later with exactly that kind of ad hoc regex/truncation fallback to make jq decidable, which the owner has already ruled out.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: close the list: either drop jq entirely from the sink set, or define it as a closed set of filters recognized syntactically (length, keys, .field|type, add, map(length)|add, etc.) with no attempt to infer scalar-ness from arbitrary jq programs. Tie head -c N to N <= OUTPUT_CAP (16384, per Q2).

findings.fix: Replace 'jq with a scalar ...' with a closed, syntactically-checkable jq filter whitelist, and cap head -c N at OUTPUT_CAP. Add GP3 rows for the boundary (curl ... | jq '.data' vs curl ... | jq 'length').

findings.title: ADR-0009's greedy ratio sort still has no stated tie-break, carried forward from r2, now also affects ADR-0016's chunk selection which reuses the same greedy shape
findings.claim: 'Take items in ratio order' (section 4) with the determinism claim '[V] 10 runs out of 10 identical' (section 5), reused by ADR-0016 as 'the same selection as ADR-0009'

archaeology.method: doc read of ADR-0009 section 4/5 and ADR-0016 'Three cases' note; grep for 'tie' / 'tie-break' in both ADRs and in DECISIONS-r3.md — no hits
archaeology.introduced_by: doc-only, raised at r2 (out/r2/round1/review/algorithms.json, finding at ADR-0009:73) for the session-state block only
archaeology.original_intent: a deterministic function of the journal so the same rows always render the same bytes
archaeology.regression_risk: now that ADR-0016 explicitly imports this greedy shape for BM25 chunk selection under OUTPUT_CAP, the missing tie-break also applies to subagent chunk output: two chunks with equal BM25 score and equal byte size have no defined order, so which chunk the subagent sees first (and whether it is cut off by the budget before the second) is not reproducible across runs. The r3/r4 decisions (Q2, Q12) fixed the budget number but not the ordering rule.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: state one explicit total order in ADR-0009 (e.g. ratio desc, then seq desc) and have ADR-0016 state it inherits that exact rule, not just 'the same selection' in prose.

findings.fix: Add 'ties broken by seq descending' to ADR-0009 section 4, and add one line to ADR-0016 confirming chunk ties use the identical rule, with a GP3 case of two equal-score chunks.

ALG-R4B-002 is a finding against missing determinism detail, not a proposal to change OUTPUT_CAP=16384 (Q2) or the budgeted-greedy mechanism itself.
